info.name: Omu API
info.description:
Omu is a small social network: accounts, posts (280 chars), replies, reposts, likes, bookmarks, follows, home/explore timelines, hashtags, search and notifications.

**Run it top to bottom** with the Collection Runner (folders are ordered so each step has the data it needs). Tokens and ids are saved to collection variables by test scripts. Two users (A and B) are created so social flows work.

Set `base_url` in the *Omu Local* environment (default `http://localhost:3000`).

**Conventions**
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (collection-level, inherited).
- Lists: `{ "data": [...], "next_cursor": <id|null> }`; pass `?limit=` (1-100) and `?cursor=`.
- Errors: `{ "error": "..." }`; validation errors add `"fields": {...}` (422).

request.description: Service name and version.
Runs `SELECT 1` against PostgreSQL.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Registration issues an opaque bearer token. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; only its SHA-256 is stored server-side.

request.description: Creates account **A** and stores its bearer token in `{{token}}`. A random username is generated on first run. Username: 3-15 letters/digits/underscores. Password: 8-72 bytes.
Creates a second account **B** (token in `{{token_b}}`) so follow, like, repost and notification flows can be exercised.
Each invalid field is reported under `fields`.
Usernames and emails are unique, case-insensitively.
`login` accepts a username or an email. Returns a fresh token (stored in `{{token_login}}`).
Revokes only the token used for this request.
`email` is visible only on your own profile.
All fields optional. An empty `avatar_url` clears it. Bio max 160, display name max 50.
Public. `following` / `follows_you` are relative to the caller when a token is sent.
Prefix match on username or display name.
Popular accounts you don't follow yet.
Idempotent. Creates a `follow` notification for B.
B follows A, which creates a `follow` notification for A and puts A's posts in B's home feed.
Paginated: `?limit=20&cursor=<next_cursor>`.
Max 280 characters. `#hashtags` are indexed; `@mentions` notify the mentioned user.

exec: pm.test("Body saved and author set", () => { pm.expect(j.body).to.include("Hello Omu"); pm.expect(j.author.username).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("username")); });

request.description: `parent_id` makes it a reply. Notifies the parent's author.
Public. `liked` / `reposted` / `bookmarked` reflect the caller when a token is sent.
Oldest first. Paginate with `cursor` = last reply's `entry_id`.
Idempotent: liking twice still counts once.
Appears in B's followers' home feeds with `reposted_by`.
Bookmarks are private.
Posts and reposts from you and everyone you follow, newest first. Replies are excluded. Pagination: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`.

exec: pm.test("Has B's post and B's repost of A's post", () => { const ids = j.data.map(p => p.id); pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("post_b_id")); });
pm.test("Replies are excluded", () => pm.expect(j.data.every(p => p.parent_id === null)).to.eql(true));

request.description: All public posts. Sends your token if set, so the flags are personalised.
Set `replies=true` to include their replies.
Case-insensitive substring search; `%` and `_` are matched literally.
Kinds: `follow`, `like`, `repost`, `reply`, `mention`. You are never notified about your own actions.

exec: pm.test("Contains like, repost, reply and follow kinds", () => { const k = j.data.map(n => n.kind); ["like","repost","reply","follow"].forEach(x => pm.expect(k).to.include(x)); });

request.description: Only the author can delete.
Signs out every other session of this user; the current token stays valid.
Cascades to the post's replies, reposts, likes and bookmarks.
